newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says probing $1.4 bln fraud, laundering.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says probing $1.4 bln fraud, laundering.

text.p: Brazil's Attorney General Geraldo Brindeiro has ordered an investigation into possible exchange rate fraud and money laundering totalling $1.4 billion via accounts at Banco do Brasil and three other banks, an Attorney General's office spokesman said.
The spokesman said Brindeiro has asked federal police and three prosecutors to probe "irregularities" detailed in a Central Bank report involving cross-border transactions with Paraguay.

According to the Central Bank, fraud and laundering may have taken place in the first quarter of this year through checking accounts at Banco do Brasil, Banco do Estado de Minas Gerais, Banco Araucaria and Banco do Estado do Parana.
Officials at the banks were not immediately available for comment.
The banks are authorized to conduct cross-border transactions between Paraguay and Brazil, the spokesman said.
The issue is worrisome to Central Bank officials, who are concerned about the outflow of dollars because of a deteriorating current account balance of payments deficit, he added.
